title: Role sprawl detection, SSO assertion fuzzing, and audit-forwarding remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Recent external pen-test and internal threat review highlighted three correlated gaps: role sprawl (large number of long-lived roles and policy attachments), insufficient SSO/SAML assertion validation under malformed/fuzzed inputs, and gaps in audit-forwarding for admin-sensitive events. This ticket houses the remediation design, implementation plan, and verification steps for those items as part of RBAC v2 Hardening.

Objectives:
- Implement automated detection for role sprawl and orphaned policies, with actionable signals and bulk remediation UI/CLI.
- Build and run an SSO/SAML assertion fuzzing harness to reproduce pen-test findings and harden assertion parsing/validation.
- Ensure audit-forwarding architecture reliably includes admin-sensitive events (role changes, SSO config updates, critical token grants) to SIEM with schema versioning and replay protection.

Deliverables:
1) Role sprawl detector: DB-backed scan job + alerting rules. Rules include thresholds (e.g., >15 principals, >90 days no-activity, >3 policy attachments) and heuristics (service-account-like naming). Output: CSV export, remediation PR template, UI link to bulk-deactivate.
2) Fuzzing harness and fixes: A small test harness that runs both structured mutation and random fuzz against SAML assertions (signature edge cases, missing Conditions/Audience, clock skews, replay). Fixes include stricter audience binding, explicit Conditions validation, rejection of ambiguous NameID formats, and limiting accepted clock skew to 30s for admin flows.
3) Audit-forwarding guarantees: Extend event pipeline to mark admin events as high-fidelity, include event_id, prev_state diff, actor metadata, and ensure at-least-once delivery to SIEM (kafka topic redelivery handling + observability dashboard). Add schema v2 and migration plan.

Acceptance criteria:
- Role sprawl detector runs daily, creates alerts for top-10 risky roles, and a remediation path exists through Console and CLI.
- Fuzzing harness reproduces at least 3 distinct assertion failures reported in pen-test and new fixes are covered by unit/integration tests.
- Admin events are visible in SIEM with >99.9% delivery rate over 7-day window in canary region, and an auditor can trace a role-change event to the originating API key/session.

Risks & mitigations:
- False positives in role sprawl detector: start with conservative thresholds, require manual approval for bulk actions.
- SAML parsing regressions: ship fixes behind feature flag for canary customers and run cross-tenant SSO e2e tests.
- Event amplification/duplication in SIEM: include idempotency keys and dedupe logic in SIEM connector.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: implement detector job + basic Console UI link (internal alpha).
- Week 2: deliver fuzzing harness and initial SAML validation fixes behind flag; run against staging and pen-test harness.
- Week 3: extend pipeline for audit-forwarding schema v2; run canary to 10% of accounts with dedicated dashboards.
- Week 4: full rollout and post-ship verification, update runbooks.

Metrics to monitor:
- Number of detected risky roles and remediation rate (% resolved).
- SAML assertion rejection rate by error bucket (before/after).
- SIEM delivery success rate and latency for admin events.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/Security/RBACv2+Hardening
- Fuzz harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security-fuzzing/pulls/27
- RBAC changes PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/984
- Pen-test summary (redacted): https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/pen-test-2025-rbac.pdf

Notes: This ticket bundles multiple related remediation actions to preserve context between SSO hardening, RBAC hygiene, and observability. If work breadth becomes too large, split into child issues for the detector, the SAML fixes, and the audit pipeline change.
